message.content: {"caption":"A left-to-right process diagram showing a Repair workflow that rejects an iteration, reverts to its initial state, and later reaches passing checks.","description":"Five rounded boxes are connected by four thin gray arrows pointing from left to right; the arrows have no labels. The first box shows S₀, 188 lines, and “Repair locked.” The second, outlined in red, is labeled “Iter. 1” and shows τw 12/13 FAIL in red and τwo 13/13 PASS in blue. The third, outlined in red, says “Revert,” “back to S₀” in red, and “iterator not called”; S₀ refers to the initial state. The fourth, outlined in blue, is labeled “Iter. 3,” shows 48 lines, τw 13/13 PASS in blue, and τwo 12/13 FAIL in red. The final blue-outlined box is labeled “Iter. 5,” shows 50 lines, “13/13 PASS” in blue, and “verbatim label.” The sequence therefore goes from a locked 188-line starting state, through a failed first iteration and rollback, to passing τw at iteration 3 and a 13/13 pass with a verbatim label at iteration 5.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
